name: Number of graphs with n vertices that have no induced regular subgraph of order 6 or greater.
comment: By Ramsey's Theorem, this sequence eventually becomes zero. It is known that a(20) is large, but it is not known whether a(21) is zero or positive.
For the analogous sequences counting graphs with no induced regular subgraph of order k or greater, the location where the sequence becomes zero is known for all k < 6.
link: Paul W. Dyson and Brendan D. McKay, Ramsey numbers for regular induced subgraphs, arXiv:2604.08215 [math.CO] (2026).
Paul Dyson and Brendan McKay, Ramsey Graphs (section Regular induced subgraphs)

example: Of all 6-vertex graphs, 148 avoid regular induced subgraphs of order 6 or more.
